docs.title: Z13GUI+: Power, Thermals & RGB Drawer for the ASUS ROG Flow Z13 on Linux
docs.text:
An Armoury Crate–style control drawer for the 2025 ASUS ROG Flow Z13 (Ryzen AI Max / Strix Halo) on Linux. It adapts to the hardware it finds, so other AMD Strix Halo machines work with the controls they actually have (experimental). Control performance profiles, TDP, fan curves, undervolt, RGB lighting, battery charge limit, and refresh rate from a touch- and gamepad-friendly GTK4 overlay on KDE Plasma, other Wayland desktops, and Steam Gaming Mode. Powered by the z13ctl-plus daemon.

Z13GUI+ is an independently named fork of dahui/z13gui targeting z13ctl-plus. It preserves intentional API and UI compatibility, not runtime-name compatibility. Starting with v2.0.0, the command, service, configuration/runtime paths, desktop and udev filenames, GApplication ID, and Go module all use the Plus namespace. The only installed command is z13gui-plus.

docs.title: What Plus Adds
docs.text:
• Power automation — save named configurations, assign separate plugged-in and battery presets, and apply them automatically when the power source changes
  • Independent CPU policy — control minimum CPU frequency, AMD EPP, and boost without coupling them to GPU clocks
  • Expanded telemetry — monitor CPU, GPU, NPU, memory, battery, power, clocks, temperatures, and both fans from a dedicated Overview
  • Battery insight — see health, energy capacity, system draw, charge state, and direction-aware runtime estimates
  • Direct display control — switch the internal panel between 60 Hz and 180 Hz
  • Safer tuning feedback — identify unsaved overrides, high-TDP fan safety, the live fan-curve operating point, and reset all tuning overrides together
  • Faster fan control — select Auto, Balanced, or Turbo without editing a curve

Hardware-control changes are sent through the z13ctl-plus daemon.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Wayland compositor with layer-shell support, or gamescope (Steam Gaming Mode). GNOME works through a beta overlay backend.
  • GTK 4 and gtk4-layer-shell libraries (see Installation for distro package names)
  • z13ctl-plus daemon running

The Plus and upstream packages can coexist. Installation does not enable the GUI service or manage either controller service; explicitly enable only the GUI that matches your selected daemon.

docs.title: GNOME support (beta)
docs.text:
Untested beta

GNOME support has not been tested by the maintainer. It ships so GNOME users can try it; please report what works and what does not in an issue.

GNOME's compositor (Mutter) does not implement the layer-shell protocol the drawer normally uses to anchor itself to the screen edge, and installing gtk4-layer-shell cannot add it. When layer-shell is missing on a Wayland session, Z13GUI+ selects the overlay backend automatically: a transparent, monitor-sized window with the drawer against the right edge. Everything outside the drawer is click-through, so the desktop stays usable. The startup log says using the overlay backend (BETA...) when it is active.

Compared with KDE Plasma, Hyprland or Sway:

  • The drawer is an ordinary window, so it is not drawn above fullscreen apps and belongs to the current workspace.
  • It may appear in Alt-Tab while open (it is unmapped when closed).
  • There is no click-outside backdrop: dismiss with Escape, the Armoury Crate button, or by clicking another window.

X11 sessions are not supported by this backend.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:

  • Quick Start — open the drawer and explore the controls
  • Configuration — config file, environment variables
  • Theming — built-in themes and custom color definitions

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: All notable changes. Newest first. Bodies mirror the GitHub release notes; release-notes.md (gitignored) is the scratch file for the next entry.

docs.title: v2.7.0 (2026-10-18)
docs.text: • GNOME support (beta, untested). On Wayland compositors without layer-shell, such as GNOME/Mutter, the drawer now opens through a transparent click-through overlay instead of a stuck window in the middle of the screen. Ported from upstream z13gui by @Cyb3rDudu (#2). Not yet confirmed on real GNOME hardware; reports welcome. X11 sessions keep the previous behaviour.

docs.title: v2.6.2 (2026-10-17)
docs.text:
• Tablet Kit panel: each toggle's description is now shown under it (tooltips never appear on touch), and the two-finger hold text sits under its own toggle.
  • "Keep my display scale" is renamed "Keep scale across postures".
  • The separate Touchscreen, Touch scrolling and Touchpad status rows are merged into notes under the related settings.
  • Scroll sliders gain 1 to 5 tick marks and dim while touch scrolling is off; Reset Scroll Defaults is disabled when already at the defaults.
  • Health reads "Healthy · 36 seconds ago".

docs.title: v2.6.1 (2026-10-16)
docs.text: • Fix the double red border on a focused active tab: the focus ring now replaces the active underline instead of drawing over it.

docs.title: v2.6.0 (2026-10-16)
docs.text:
Hardware hiding needs z13ctl-plus v2.5.0 (API v1.9.0); older daemons keep showing every control.

  • Power tab reordered: Profile, Fan mode, a one-tap CPU Boost row, Power automation, Battery strategy, then a single Power tuning row.
  • Power tuning is split into TDP, Fan, UV and CPU pages with pinned Save and Reset, a Simple/Advanced TDP control, compact slider rows, a compact fan graph, and warnings shown only when they apply. Minimum frequency and energy preference moved to the CPU page.
  • Overview is tiered: status strip, thermals and load, APU power against PL1, and fans, then Details with memory, clocks and a compact battery card that shows capacity left.
  • Settings (renamed from System): Boot Sound joins Display, and a folded Layout card hides any card. Battery, RGB, CPU Boost, fan, TDP and display controls hide automatically when the machine lacks the hardware.
  • RGB device picker is a segmented control; the Effect card hides while lighting is off. The tab bar uses an underline for the active tab.
  • Chakra Petch (SIL OFL) is embedded as the display face for buttons, tabs and labels.

docs.title: v2.5.0 (2026-10-13)
docs.text:
The new display notes need z13ctl-plus v2.4.0; older daemons keep the previous behaviour.

  • The DISPLAY card says which screen the refresh buttons drive. With an external display on it reads "Built-in panel: 180 Hz. Other displays aren't affected."; docked with the built-in panel off, the buttons are greyed out and the note says so. The old "firmware does not report" note was wrong and now reads "The current rate can't be read".
  • Every action reports failures on the status line; writes on the RGB and System tabs used to fail silently. Single-tap controls confirm with "Applied".
  • Power tab: one fixed feedback line at the bottom of the drawer, so status text no longer reflows the cards above it.
  • CPU Boost is an always-visible row at the top of the CPU & Power Tuning card. The collapsible header shows an explicit EXPAND label.
  • Dim text meets WCAG AA (4.5:1) on every theme, custom theme.toml included; the inactive RGB effect card is easier to read; Overview numerals use one style.
  • Removed duplicated readouts: the PROFILE and EFFECT pills, preset names repeating their row, and battery percentages shown twice.
  • Preset chips show full names, with a tooltip; the preset Reapply button meets the 40 px touch floor, now guarded by a test.

docs.title: v2.4.0 (2026-10-13)
docs.text:
Requires z13ctl-plus v2.3.0 or newer.

  • Power Automation card gets one-tap preset chips: tap to apply, the active preset is highlighted, and presets above 75 W sustained TDP are flagged before the tap.
  • A single Presets screen replaces the separate library and chooser: each preset has Apply / Edit and inline AC / Battery assignment toggles. "+ Save Current Settings" names the preset automatically.
  • Presets are now editable: profile, TDP (default or PL1/PL2/PL3), undervolt, CPU minimum/EPP/boost, refresh rate and panel overdrive. Renaming keeps assignments. Leaving with unsaved changes asks first.
  • When a manual change overrides the assigned preset, the card shows a MANUAL pill and a "Reapply " button; while automation is off, a hint names the preset that turning it on will apply.
  • Preset status and partial-apply errors show on the main card and in the editor.
  • Presets no longer show a fan-mode row (presets no longer carry fan mode).
  • KDE Plasma: Meta+Z toggles the drawer (default global shortcut, rebindable under System Settings → Shortcuts → Z13GUI+). Takes effect after the next login.

docs.title: v2.3.0 (2026-10-12)
docs.text:
• Energy-preference picker now only offers the values the kernel accepts. amd-pstate-epp advertises the allowed EPP values per current cpufreq policy — under the performance policy that is performance alone. All four buttons used to render regardless; the daemon rejected the rest (unsupported CPU EPP) and, because the failure was only reported in the Presets view, the picker silently snapped back to Performance. Buttons now follow the daemon's epp_choices (the kernel's advertised list) and repopulate live whenever the policy changes.
  • New Dynamic energy preference on Linux 7.3+ kernels: amd-pstate-epp's dynamic mode lets the kernel pick the EPP from the power source / platform profile natively. The button only appears when the kernel advertises it, so older kernels are unaffected.
  • Fixed the active highlight in dynamic mode: the 7.3 kernel reads dynamic back as dynamic(profile:…), which previously matched no button (nothing turned red) and leaked into the tuning summary and presets captured from live state. The suffix is now stripped at every consumption point.

docs.title: v2.2.1 (2026-10-12)
docs.text:
• System tab: new ABOUT card showing the installed versions of Z13GUI+, Z13CTL+, and z13-tablet-kit.
  • Switches no longer freeze halfway when the periodic state refresh lands while you are toggling them.

docs.title: v2.2.0 (2026-10-12)
docs.text:
• Tablet Kit panel: new "Keep my display scale" toggle. When on, z13ctl-plus never changes the screen scale on posture changes. Requires z13ctl-plus v2.2.1. z13-tablet-kit#1
  • KDE Plasma: the hidden drawer now really stops blocking clicks on a monitor to the right of the Z13 screen (the v2.1.2 fix was not enough on KWin). While hidden the drawer drops below all windows. #1 (thanks @Sarpar12)
  • With a monitor to the right, the drawer no longer alternates between fading and sliding across that monitor on every other open.

docs.title: v2.1.2 (2026-10-11)
docs.text: • KDE Plasma: the hidden drawer no longer blocks mouse clicks on a monitor placed to the right of the Z13 screen. The invisible parked drawer is now click-through while hidden. #1 (thanks @Sarpar12)

docs.title: v2.1.1 (2026-10-11)
docs.text:
• Gaming Mode: closing and quickly reopening the drawer no longer lets controller input reach Steam and the game while the drawer is open.
  • RGB lighting changes run in the background (no UI freeze), revert when the daemon rejects them, and can no longer be undone by a stale state refresh.
  • The battery badge shows "—" instead of "MAX LIFE · 0%" when the charge limit is unknown.
  • The release pipeline runs the full test suite before building packages.

docs.title: v2.1.0 (2026-10-11)
docs.text:
• Tablet integration with z13-tablet-kit: a live posture and health chip (hidden until the kit reports a heartbeat) with toggles for desktop touch policy, folio touchpad opt-in, and scroll sensitivity/speed.
  • Two-finger-hold context menu toggle.
  • The AUR package provides and conflicts with the tarball package name.

docs.title: v2.0.2 (2026-08-03)
docs.text: • Detached lighting devices show as off and their toggle is disabled, while the saved state is kept for when they are reattached. Requires z13ctl-plus v2.0.1.

docs.title: v2.0.1 (2026-08-03)
docs.text: • The desktop entry sets StartupNotify=false, so Plasma no longer shows a startup spinner that swallowed launcher clicks. Rapid launcher clicks now toggle the drawer reliably.

docs.title: v2.0.0 (2026-08-02)
docs.text:
Independent application identity; targets the z13ctl-plus controller only.

  • The command is z13gui-plus; no z13gui alias is installed.
  • The user unit is z13gui-plus.service; the application ID and desktop file are io.github.aic0d3r.z13gui_plus.
  • Configuration moves to $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/z13gui-plus; runtime files move to $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/z13gui-plus.
  • Environment overrides are Z13GUI_PLUS_SCALE and Z13GUI_PLUS_NO_GAMEPAD.
  • Packages coexist with upstream, depend on z13ctl-plus, and leave the GUI service disabled after installation.
  • z13gui-plus --migrate-config copies the v1 configuration into the new location without overwriting or deleting anything.

docs.title: v1.3.0 (2026-07-28)
docs.text:
First release under the z13gui-plus distribution name.

  • Overview tab with live CPU, GPU, VRAM, NPU, battery, thermal, and fan telemetry.
  • CPU power controls (minimum frequency, EPP, boost), named presets, and AC/battery power automation.
  • Tarball, Arch, Debian, RPM, and AUR packages.
  • Expanded RGB, fan, TDP, refresh-rate, and battery controls with safer input handling; refined touch-first navigation, tuning feedback, color controls, and gamepad and touchscreen handling in desktop and Gaming Mode.

docs.title: v1.0.0 – v1.2.7
docs.text: Released as dahui/z13gui before this fork. See the upstream releases.

docs.title: Config file
docs.text:
Z13GUI+ stores its configuration in $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/z13gui-plus/config.toml, normally ~/.config/z13gui-plus/config.toml. This file is updated automatically when you change themes using the in-app theme picker.

theme = "catppuccin-mocha"
accent = "sapphire"
Key Description theme Built-in theme ID (see z13gui-plus --list-themes or Theming) accent Accent color variant for themes that support it; "" uses the theme default hidden Comma-separated card IDs switched off in Settings → Layout, e.g. "overview.fans,tab.rgb". Cards for hardware the machine lacks are hidden automatically and are not listed here

If no config file exists, Z13GUI+ defaults to the rog-dark theme.

You can edit this file by hand. Changes take effect the next time Z13GUI+ starts.

docs.title: Theme priority
docs.text: See Theme priority for the resolution order and custom-theme behavior.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text: Variable Description Z13GUI_PLUS_SCALE Override CSS scale factor in gamescope mode (default: auto from output resolution) Z13GUI_PLUS_NO_GAMEPAD Set to 1 to disable gamepad input entirely

docs.title: Command-line flags
docs.text:
Flag Description --debug, -d Enable debug logging (includes GTK messages) --version Print version and exit --print-theme Print the default theme.toml to stdout --list-themes List all built-in theme IDs and names --migrate-config Copy the complete legacy v1 config directory into the Plus namespace; fails if the Plus config already exists

--print-theme is the recommended starting point for a custom theme:

mkdir -p ~/.config/z13gui-plus
z13gui-plus --print-theme > ~/.config/z13gui-plus/theme.toml

For v1 configuration, use the explicit migration command. Do not manually merge the old and new directories.

docs.title: Runtime files
docs.text: Z13GUI+ keeps its owned runtime files under $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/z13gui-plus. If XDG_RUNTIME_DIR is unavailable, the embedded-font cache falls back to /tmp/z13gui-plus/fonts, while Steam frozen-process recovery follows the existing per-user convention at /run/user/$UID/z13gui-plus/frozen-pid.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: Contributions are welcome. Please open an issue before starting work on a significant change so the approach can be discussed first.

docs.title: Repository structure
docs.text:
The root module is github.com/aic0d3r/z13gui-plus. Z13GUI+ intentionally continues to import the controller API as github.com/dahui/z13ctl/api; the go.mod replacement selects github.com/aic0d3r/z13ctl-plus/api, whose client targets the Plus socket. Do not change the import to a fork-specific path or remove the replacement.

Package Purpose internal/gui Main Window type, daemon subscription, gamepad navigation internal/gui/layershell Wayland layer-shell display backend internal/gui/gamescope X11 overlay backend for Steam Gaming Mode internal/gui/overlay Beta overlay backend for Wayland without layer-shell (GNOME) internal/panelgeom Overlay panel geometry and slide easing — pure Go internal/gui/gamepad Linux evdev gamepad reader internal/gui/gamepad/hidblocker BPF LSM hidraw blocker (blocks PS/Nintendo controller reads) internal/gui/fonts Embedded Inter and Chakra Petch (OFL) font registration internal/theme Color definitions, TOML parsing, CSS generation — pure Go

docs.title: Development setup
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/aic0d3r/z13gui-plus
cd z13gui-plus

Build dependencies (Arch Linux):

sudo pacman -S gtk4 gtk4-layer-shell

Build dependencies (Debian/Ubuntu):

sudo apt-get install -y libgtk-4-dev libgtk4-layer-shell-dev

Build dependencies (Fedora):

sudo dnf install gtk4-devel gtk4-layer-shell-devel

BPF development (optional — only for modifying the hidraw blocker):

Requires clang, bpftool, and kernel BTF support.

make vmlinux   # generate kernel BTF header
make generate  # compile BPF and generate Go bindings

To work against a local copy of the z13ctl-plus API module, create a go.work file (it is gitignored; adjust the sibling directory name if needed):

go work init . ../z13ctl-plus/api

docs.title: Before submitting a pull request
docs.text:
make build     # compile (requires GTK4 headers)
make lint      # run golangci-lint
make test      # run unit tests (pure Go, no GTK4 required)

Tests live in the pure-Go packages (internal/theme, internal/togglegate) — no hardware or GTK4 dependency. GUI packages are integration-tested manually against hardware.

make test lists those packages explicitly instead of using ./..., since internal/gui requires CGO and GTK4 headers. If you add a new pure-Go package with tests, add it to the test and cover targets in the Makefile or its tests will never run.

Pull requests must pass make build, make lint, and make test without errors, and should include tests for any changes to the pure-Go packages.

docs.title: Testing notes
docs.text:
• internal/theme — fully unit-testable; covers color parsing, CSS generation, config persistence, and all 78 built-in theme/accent combinations
  • internal/togglegate — pure debounce helper for duplicate gui-toggle bursts
  • internal/gui — requires GTK4; integration-tested manually against hardware
  • internal/panelgeom — pure Go; covers the overlay panel rectangle and slide
  • Display backends (layershell, gamescope, overlay) — require a compositor or gamescope; no automated tests

docs.title: Release workflow (maintainers only)
docs.text:
git tag -a v2.0.0 -F release-notes.md
git push origin v2.0.0

GoReleaser handles binary builds, the .pkg.tar.zst, .deb, and .rpm packages, AUR publishing, and GitHub Release creation automatically when the tag is pushed. v2.0.0 is the independently named Plus namespace release; release notes must not claim shared runtime-name compatibility with upstream.

docs.title: Opening the drawer
docs.text:
Press the Armoury Crate button on your Z13. The drawer slides in from the right edge of the screen.

Press it again, click anywhere outside the drawer, or press Escape to close it.

docs.title: Drawer controls
docs.text:
Section What it does Overview Status, temperatures and load, APU power against the sustained limit, and fans, then memory, clocks, and battery under Details. Profile Switch between quiet, balanced, and performance hardware profiles. Power Automation Assign named presets to plugged-in and battery operation. Each row shows what the preset sets. Tap a preset chip to apply it now; a MANUAL badge and Reapply button appear after manual changes. Manage Presets lists every preset with Apply, Edit, and Plugged In / On Battery assignment buttons, plus Save Current Settings (named automatically; rename in Edit). The editor covers name, profile, TDP, undervolt, CPU behavior, refresh rate, and overdrive. Fan mode is never part of a preset. CPU Boost One-tap switch on the Power tab. Power Tuning Open the tuning view: TDP (Simple or Advanced PL1/PL2/PL3), fan curve, undervolt, and CPU (minimum frequency and EPP) pages, each with its own Save and Reset. Fan Mode Select firmware Auto or the Balanced and Turbo curve presets. Battery Limit Set the charge cap (40–100%). Changes persist across reboots. Refresh Rate Switch the internal display between 60 Hz and 180 Hz. Keyboard / Lightbar Tab between the two lighting zones Mode Lighting effect: static, breathe, cycle, rainbow, strobe, or off Color 1 / Color 2 Pick from 8 presets or open the custom color picker Speed Animation speed for modes that support it: slow, normal, fast Brightness Lighting brightness: low, medium, or high Layout In Settings, hide cards you do not need. Cards for hardware the machine lacks are hidden automatically. Panel Overdrive Toggle faster pixel response (may cause slight ghosting) Boot Sound Enable or disable the startup POST sound Tablet kit chip When the optional tablet companion is detected, open its posture, health, touchscreen, touchpad, and scrolling controls.

Changes take effect immediately and are sent to the z13ctl-plus daemon. Saved device settings persist across reboots; CPU power controls reflect live kernel state.

The tablet kit chip is absent until the optional companion reports its first heartbeat. Healthy operation stays unobtrusive; companion errors and stale heartbeats put the chip in a warning state. Enabling the GZ302EA folio touchpad always asks for confirmation because affected firmware can cause a jumping cursor. The optional two-finger hold setting opens the context menu after holding two stationary fingers briefly; moving fingers scrolls and cancels it. "Keep my display scale" stops posture changes from touching the screen scale.

The theme picker button at the bottom-left of the drawer opens the theme view. See Theming for details.

docs.title: Custom color picker
docs.text: Click Custom under any color input to open the HSL color picker. Adjust the Hue, Saturation, and Lightness sliders to dial in any color. The preview swatch updates in real time.

docs.title: Gamepad navigation
docs.text:
Z13GUI+ supports full gamepad control for use in Steam Gaming Mode:

Input Action D-pad Navigate between controls A (Cross) Activate buttons/switches, or enter edit mode for sliders Left/Right (in edit mode) Adjust a slider value A (in edit mode) Commit the value B (Circle) Cancel edit, go back, or close the drawer L1/R1 (shoulder) Jump between sections

Gamepad focus (indicated by a highlight border) is automatically hidden when the mouse moves. To disable gamepad input entirely, set Z13GUI_PLUS_NO_GAMEPAD=1.

docs.title: Gamescope (Steam Gaming Mode)
docs.text:
In Steam Gaming Mode, Z13GUI+ runs as a gamescope X11 overlay. The backend is selected automatically when GAMESCOPE_WAYLAND_DISPLAY is set and its socket is present.

The UI scales automatically to match the output resolution. Use Z13GUI_PLUS_SCALE to override the auto-detected scale factor if the UI appears too large or small.

Theme and color controls use full-view alternatives on every backend because gamescope does not composite separate popup windows.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Linux kernel (x86_64)
  • Wayland compositor with layer-shell support, or gamescope (Steam Gaming Mode). GNOME uses an untested beta overlay backend.
  • z13ctl-plus installed with its Plus daemon running

docs.title: Runtime dependencies
docs.text:
Z13GUI+ links dynamically against GTK 4 and gtk4-layer-shell. The AUR package pulls these automatically; for other install methods, install them via your system package manager first.

Dependency Arch Debian / Ubuntu Fedora GTK 4 gtk4 libgtk-4-1 gtk4 gtk4-layer-shell gtk4-layer-shell libgtk4-layer-shell0 gtk4-layer-shell

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Release binaryArch Linux (AUR)Debian / UbuntuFedora / RHELFrom source

Install the runtime dependencies for your distro, then download the latest linux_amd64 archive from the Releases page:

tar xzf z13gui-plus_*_linux_amd64.tar.gz
sudo install -Dm755 z13gui-plus /usr/local/bin/z13gui-plus
sudo install -Dm644 contrib/io.github.aic0d3r.z13gui_plus.desktop \
    /usr/local/share/applications/io.github.aic0d3r.z13gui_plus.desktop
sudo install -Dm644 contrib/70-z13gui-plus-gamepad.rules \
    /etc/udev/rules.d/70-z13gui-plus-gamepad.rules

Install the systemd user service:

install -Dm644 contrib/z13gui-plus.service \
    ~/.config/systemd/user/z13gui-plus.service
systemctl --user daemon-reload
systemctl --user enable --now z13gui-plus.service

Install the z13gui-plus-bin package with your preferred AUR helper:

yay -S z13gui-plus-bin

This package depends on z13ctl-plus-bin. It installs the binary, systemd service, udev rules, and desktop entry, but leaves the GUI service disabled and does not enable or manage the controller service. Enable the GUI after selecting the Plus daemon:

systemctl --user enable --now z13gui-plus.service

Alternatively, download the .pkg.tar.zst package directly from the Releases page and install with pacman:

sudo pacman -U z13gui-plus-*.pkg.tar.zst

Download the .deb package from the Releases page, then install:

sudo apt install ./z13gui-plus_*.deb

The package depends on z13ctl-plus and installs the binary, systemd service, udev rules, and desktop entry. It leaves the GUI service disabled and does not manage controller services. After selecting the Plus daemon, enable the GUI:

systemctl --user enable --now z13gui-plus.service

Download the .rpm package from the Releases page, then install:

sudo dnf install ./z13gui-plus_*.rpm

The package depends on z13ctl-plus and installs the binary, systemd service, udev rules, and desktop entry. It leaves the GUI service disabled and does not manage controller services. After selecting the Plus daemon, enable the GUI:

systemctl --user enable --now z13gui-plus.service

Requires Go 1.25+, CGO enabled, and GTK4 development libraries.

Arch Linux:

sudo pacman -S gtk4 gtk4-layer-shell

Debian/Ubuntu:

sudo apt-get install -y libgtk-4-dev libgtk4-layer-shell-dev

Fedora:

sudo dnf install gtk4-devel gtk4-layer-shell-devel

Then clone and build:

git clone https://github.com/aic0d3r/z13gui-plus
cd z13gui-plus
make build
sudo make install
sudo setcap cap_bpf,cap_perfmon+ep /usr/local/bin/z13gui-plus
make install-service

make build creates ./z13gui-plus; it does not create an unqualified compatibility binary.

docs.title: Package coexistence and service selection
docs.text:
z13gui-plus is independently named and can be installed alongside upstream z13gui. Plus packages do not provide, conflict with, or replace upstream. Package installation never enables the GUI service and never starts, stops, or enables a controller service.

Select the z13ctl-plus daemon separately, then explicitly enable only its matching GUI:

systemctl --user enable --now z13ctl-plus.socket
systemctl --user enable --now z13gui-plus.service

Do not enable z13gui-plus.service for an upstream controller daemon. The canonical controller API import is replaced with the fork API source and targets only the Plus socket.

docs.title: Gamepad input blocking (capabilities)
docs.text:
In Steam Gaming Mode (gamescope), Z13GUI+ suppresses controller input while the drawer is open so button presses navigate the overlay instead of the game.

Z13GUI+ supports two blocking methods and selects the best one automatically:

Method Requires Behaviour Side effects BPF blocker (preferred) CAP_BPF + CAP_PERFMON on the binary Blocks PS / Nintendo controller reads at the kernel level via a BPF LSM hook None — Steam and the game keep running normally SIGSTOP fallback No extra capabilities Pauses the Steam process with SIGSTOP / SIGCONT Game also pauses; PipeWire frame delivery stops

The AUR, .deb, and .rpm packages grant the required capabilities automatically during installation. If you installed from source or from the release binary, grant them manually:

sudo setcap cap_bpf,cap_perfmon+ep /usr/local/bin/z13gui-plus
What are these capabilities and are they safe?

docs.title: Short version
docs.text: These two capabilities let Z13GUI+ load a tiny kernel filter that tells the system "when Steam tries to read a PS or Nintendo controller, return a temporary 'try again later' error instead." That's all it does. It cannot access your files, network, or any other part of the system. The filter is automatically removed when Z13GUI+ exits.

docs.title: Technical details
docs.text:
CAP_BPF allows loading BPF programs into the kernel. Z13GUI+ uses this to attach a single LSM (lsm/file_permission) hook that intercepts read() calls on hidraw character devices (/dev/hidraw*). The hook checks whether the calling PID is in a small allow-list map and the target device is a hidraw device (major 244). If both conditions match, it returns -EAGAIN; otherwise it returns 0 (allow).

CAP_PERFMON is required by the kernel to attach BPF LSM programs. Z13GUI+ does not use performance monitoring — this capability is a kernel-imposed prerequisite for LSM attachment.

What the BPF program can do:

  • Return -EAGAIN for read() calls on hidraw devices by specific PIDs
  • Nothing else — the program is verified by the kernel's BPF verifier before loading and cannot be modified at runtime

What the BPF program cannot do:

  • Access files, network, or memory outside its own BPF maps
  • Survive a process exit — all BPF resources are released when Z13GUI+ stops, crashes, or is killed
  • Affect any process not explicitly added to its PID map
  • Block any operation other than read() on hidraw devices

Compared to running as root: file capabilities grant only the two listed privileges to the z13gui-plus binary. The process runs as your normal user with no other elevated access. This is strictly safer than running with sudo or as root.

docs.title: Verify the installation
docs.text:
z13gui-plus --version

Then press the Armoury Crate button on your Z13. The drawer should slide in from the right edge of the screen.

docs.title: Migrating from v1 to v2
docs.text:
v1 of this fork used the shared legacy z13gui namespace. v2.0.0 is independently named. After installing v2, copy the entire legacy configuration directory with:

z13gui-plus --migrate-config

The command copies $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/z13gui (normally ~/.config/z13gui) to $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/z13gui-plus (normally ~/.config/z13gui-plus) only when the Plus destination does not exist. It leaves the source directory untouched. It does not change services or remove legacy files, launchers, rules, or binaries.

If z13gui.service is known to be the v1 fork service, switch the GUI service explicitly after selecting the Plus controller daemon:

systemctl --user disable --now z13gui.service
systemctl --user enable --now z13gui-plus.service

Legacy paths are provenance-ambiguous because they may belong to upstream or to v1 of this fork. The commands above do not remove anything. Optional cleanup must be manual: remove only legacy z13gui binaries, service files, desktop files, udev rules, or config that you have verified came from this fork. Never delete a shared-looking path merely because v2 no longer uses it.

docs.title: Uninstall
docs.text:
Stop and remove the service:

make uninstall-service

Or manually:

systemctl --user disable --now z13gui-plus.service
rm -f ~/.config/systemd/user/z13gui-plus.service
systemctl --user daemon-reload

Remove manually installed Plus artifacts:

sudo rm -f /usr/local/bin/z13gui-plus
sudo rm -f /usr/local/share/applications/io.github.aic0d3r.z13gui_plus.desktop
sudo rm -f /etc/udev/rules.d/70-z13gui-plus-gamepad.rules
sudo rm -f /etc/udev/rules.d/99-z13gui-plus-gamepad.rules  # name used before v2.6

These commands do not remove or manage z13ctl-plus.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Drawer doesn't appear

Make sure the z13ctl-plus daemon socket is enabled:

systemctl --user status z13ctl-plus.socket z13ctl-plus.service

Service fails to start

Check the journal:

journalctl --user -u z13gui-plus.service -n 50

Run with debug logging to see GTK and initialization output:

z13gui-plus --debug

CachyOS: NPU shows ACTIVE but no watts or utilization

Current CachyOS kernels include an amdxdna driver with NPU power and utilization sensors. An older amdxdna-dkms module can override it with a driver that supports inference but not those sensors. Check the loaded module:

modinfo -n amdxdna

If the path contains updates/dkms, follow the z13ctl-plus NPU telemetry guidance to test the native driver with a documented rollback. Do not remove DKMS on an older kernel unless that kernel already provides its own amdxdna module.

Gamescope: controller input not suppressed while drawer is open

Grant BPF capabilities so Z13GUI+ can block controller input at the kernel level:

sudo setcap cap_bpf,cap_perfmon+ep /usr/local/bin/z13gui-plus

Without capabilities, Z13GUI+ falls back to freezing Steam (SIGSTOP), which also pauses running games.

Gamescope: drawer doesn't show

Verify GAMESCOPE_WAYLAND_DISPLAY is set and the socket exists:

echo $GAMESCOPE_WAYLAND_DISPLAY
ls "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/$GAMESCOPE_WAYLAND_DISPLAY"

If the socket is missing (stale environment from a previous Gaming Mode session), Z13GUI+ automatically falls back to Wayland layer-shell mode.

docs.title: Theming
docs.text: Z13GUI+ supports custom color themes through a simple TOML configuration file. You can also select from 15 built-in themes using the in-app theme picker.

docs.title: Theme priority
docs.text:
Z13GUI+ resolves its theme using the following priority chain. The first match wins:

  1. ~/.config/z13gui-plus/theme.toml — custom color definitions (7 hex values)
  2. ~/.config/z13gui-plus/theme.css — full CSS override (power users)
  3. ~/.config/z13gui-plus/config.toml theme = "id" — built-in theme selection
  4. Compiled-in default (ROG Dark)

If you create a theme.toml, it always takes priority over the built-in theme picker selection. Delete or rename it to return to built-in themes.

docs.title: Built-in themes
docs.text:
ID Name Type Accents catppuccin-frappe Catppuccin Frappe dark 14 variants catppuccin-latte Catppuccin Latte light 14 variants catppuccin-macchiato Catppuccin Macchiato dark 14 variants catppuccin-mocha Catppuccin Mocha dark 14 variants everforest-light Everforest Light light — github-light GitHub Light light — gruvbox-dark Gruvbox Dark dark — gruvbox-light Gruvbox Light light — nord Nord dark — one-light One Light light — rog-dark ROG Dark dark — rog-neon ROG Neon dark — rose-pine-dawn Rose Pine Dawn light — solarized-light Solarized Light light — tokyo-night Tokyo Night dark —

List all built-in themes from the command line:

z13gui-plus --list-themes

docs.title: Choosing a built-in theme
docs.text:
Click the palette button at the bottom-left of the drawer. For themes with accent variants (all four Catppuccin themes), a row of colored dots appears below the theme name in the picker.

Your selection is saved automatically to ~/.config/z13gui-plus/config.toml.

docs.title: Creating a custom theme
docs.text:
A custom theme is a TOML file with 7 color keys. Each value is a CSS hex color string (#rrggbb).

Quick start:

mkdir -p ~/.config/z13gui-plus
z13gui-plus --print-theme > ~/.config/z13gui-plus/theme.toml

This writes the default ROG Dark colors. Open the file and change the values.

File format:

# Accent color — active buttons, slider fill, checked states
accent = "#cc0000"

# Drawer background
background = "#1a1a1a"

# Surface color — button and row backgrounds
surface = "#2a2a2a"

# Alternate surface — hover state background
surface_alt = "#333333"

# Primary text color
text = "#e0e0e0"

# Dim text color — section labels, secondary descriptions
text_dim = "#888888"

# Border color — window outline and separators
border = "#444444"

Comments, inline comments, unknown keys, and missing keys are all handled gracefully. Invalid hex values are skipped; missing keys fall back to ROG Dark defaults.

The repository's example themes contain a .toml file for every built-in theme and are useful starting points.

Changes to theme.toml take effect the next time Z13GUI+ starts.

docs.title: Accent variants
docs.text:
Custom themes can define accent color variants that appear as colored dots in the theme picker. Add an [accents] section after the color keys:

accent = "#5294e2"
background = "#1b2838"
surface = "#253449"
surface_alt = "#2e3f55"
text = "#d3dae3"
text_dim = "#7c8fa0"
border = "#3b5068"

[accents]
blue = "#5294e2"
teal = "#2eb398"
purple = "#9b59b6"
orange = "#e67e22"

Each line is id = "#hex". The ID is used as the tooltip and saved to config.toml. The top-level accent key sets the default when no variant is selected.

docs.title: Color reference
docs.text: Key CSS variable Controls accent @z13-accent Active buttons, slider fill, checked radio buttons, active tab background @z13-bg Drawer panel background surface @z13-surface Button backgrounds, input row backgrounds surface_alt @z13-surface-alt Hover state for buttons and rows text @z13-text Primary text, labels, button text text_dim @z13-text-dim Section headings (MODE, SPEED, etc.), secondary labels border @z13-border Drawer border, separators, button outlines

docs.title: Full CSS override
docs.text:
For complete control, provide a full GTK4 CSS stylesheet at ~/.config/z13gui-plus/theme.css. This replaces the built-in theme CSS entirely.

The stylesheet should define all 7 @define-color variables:

@define-color z13-accent      #cc0000;
@define-color z13-bg          #1a1a1a;
@define-color z13-surface     #2a2a2a;
@define-color z13-surface-alt #333333;
@define-color z13-text        #e0e0e0;
@define-color z13-text-dim    #888888;
@define-color z13-border      #444444;

You can then add any GTK4 CSS rules. theme.toml takes priority over theme.css — delete theme.toml to use a CSS override.
